**Today's date: 2026-05-30 (UTC).**

## Research context

We are generating ideas in the area of: **Target: AAAI 2027
Track: Information Retrieval and Text Mining

Direction: Train an end-to-end visual document retrieval model that produces embeddings at three granularities (page, region, element) with explicit spatial grounding, using differentiable region proposals from intermediate VLM layers and multi-task training on page-level contrastive, element-level alignment, and spatial grounding losses. The model should close the 28.5pp page-vs-layout retrieval gap (MMDocIR) while producing bounding boxes for evidence localization (targeting >70% IoU@0.5 on ViDoRe V3, up from 59.7% baseline).

Seed Papers:
- ColPali (Faysse et al., ICLR 2025) — Established the late-interaction multi-vector paradigm for visual document retrieval; architecture base
- MMDocIR (Dong et al., EMNLP 2025) — Benchmark revealing 28.5pp gap between page-level and layout-level retrieval; provides layout annotations for training
- Spatially-Grounded Retrieval / Snappy (arXiv Dec 2025) — Inference-time patch-to-region propagation achieving 59.7% IoU@0.5; proves patch features contain spatial information but lacks learned optimization
- AGREE (Cui et al., arXiv Nov 2025) — Attention-grounded enhancement using cross-modal attention as region supervision; closest existing work but targets page-level nDCG, not element retrieval
- ColParse (Yan et al., arXiv Mar 2026) — Layout-informed sub-image embeddings achieving compression + accuracy gains; shows layout awareness helps but depends on external parser
- MURE (Zhu et al., arXiv Mar 2026) — Multi-resolution hierarchical encoding; demonstrates multi-scale helps but doesn't do element retrieval
- ViDoRe V3 (arXiv Jan 2026) — Benchmark with spatial grounding evaluation via bounding box IoU; evaluation target
- RegionGPT (Guo et al., CVPR 2024) — Region-level understanding in VLMs via differentiable region proposals; architectural inspiration for learned region extraction

Known Gaps:
- No end-to-end model performs sub-page element retrieval from raw page images without external layout detectors (ColParse needs parsers, Multi-Granularity Framework needs VLM filtering)
- Spatial grounding in visual document retrieval is limited to inference-time heuristics (59.7% IoU@0.5); no model learns to ground during training
- The 28.5pp page-vs-layout gap (MMDocIR) has no solution that doesn't introduce pipeline components

Theoretical Anchor: Vision transformer patch embeddings implicitly encode spatial layout information (evidenced by Snappy's inference-time grounding and AGREE's attention-based region discovery), but this information is never explicitly optimized during retrieval training. By introducing differentiable ROI pooling over ViT feature maps with element-level alignment supervision, we can convert implicit spatial encoding into explicit hierarchical retrieval capability — analogous to how Faster R-CNN made object detection end-to-end by replacing external proposals with learned region proposal networks.

Constraints:
- Compute: ≤200 H100-hours (LoRA fine-tuning on ColQwen2 architecture, ~100-150 hours estimated)
- Training data: MMDocIR (1,685 expert + 173K bootstrapped queries with layout annotations), DocLayNet, PubLayNet
- Evaluation: MMDocIR layout-level, ViDoRe V3 grounding (IoU@0.5), ViDoRe V2 page-level (no regression)

Quality Self-Checks:
- [x] Core insight: Patch embeddings already encode layout — training with element-level supervision makes this explicit and learnable.
- [x] Why not obvious: Requires combining differentiable region proposals (from detection literature) with late-interaction retrieval (from IR literature) — cross-community gap.
- [x] Baseline fear test: A simple baseline of "run layout detector then embed crops" exists (ColParse), but it can't jointly optimize detection and retrieval, and adds inference latency. The end-to-end model should beat it by 3-5pp on layout-level retrieval through joint optimization.
- [x] Information exploited: Intermediate VLM layer features for region proposals + element-level bounding box annotations from MMDocIR/DocLayNet — neither used by any current retrieval model during training.

Avoid:
- Relying on external document parsers or layout detectors at inference time (the whole point is end-to-end)
- Evaluating only on ViDoRe V1 (saturated; reviewers will flag this)
- Proposing yet another compression method (crowded; 6+ papers in 12 months)
- Bigger backbone scaling without architectural innovation (engineering contribution, not research)
- OCR-vs-VLM comparisons (settled question since ColPali)**

# RegionRAG: Region-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation Analysis

## Abstract Summary

The paper addresses a fundamental limitation in multi-modal RAG systems. Current approaches treat entire documents as retrieval units, introducing irrelevant visual content in two ways: documents contain large unrelated regions, and retrieving multiple documents adds redundant material that "distract[s] the model's attention."

RegionRAG proposes shifting "the retrieval paradigm from the document level to the region level." The framework achieves notable improvements: "10.02% in R@1 on average" for retrieval accuracy and "3.56% while using only 71.42% visual tokens" for question answering performance.

## Method Overview

**Training Strategy:**
The system employs "a hybrid supervision strategy from both labeled data and unlabeled data to pinpoint relevant patches," enabling the model to learn which visual regions are query-relevant.

**Inference Pipeline:**
During inference, the framework implements "a dynamic pipeline that intelligently groups salient patches into complete semantic regions." By delegating region identification to the retriever, the generator can "focus solely on concise, query-relevant visual content, improving both efficiency and accuracy."

## Key Innovation

The core contribution centers on shifting from document-level to region-level retrieval granularity, reducing irrelevant visual information while maintaining or improving answer quality.

---

# VisRAG: Vision-based Retrieval-augmented Generation Summary

## Abstract

The paper introduces VisRAG, a system that addresses limitations in traditional RAG by leveraging vision capabilities. As stated in the abstract, "current RAG systems are solely based on text, rendering it impossible to utilize vision information like layout and images that play crucial roles in real-world multi-modality documents."

The core innovation involves using a vision-language model (VLM) to directly embed documents as images rather than parsing them into text first. This approach "maximizes the retention and utilization of the data information in the original documents, eliminating the information loss introduced during the parsing process."

# VisRAG Technical Method and Architecture

## Core System Design

VisRAG implements a vision-based RAG pipeline with two main components: a retriever (VisRAG-Ret) and a generator (VisRAG-Gen). Unlike traditional text-based RAG systems that parse documents into text segments, VisRAG directly processes document pages as images using vision-language models.

## Retrieval Architecture

**Dual-Encoder Approach:**
VisRAG-Ret follows the dual-encoder paradigm from dense retrieval models but substitutes a VLM for the typical language model. Both queries and document pages are encoded separately—queries as text and pages as images—producing sequences of hidden states through the VLM.

**Embedding Generation:**
Final embeddings are derived using "position-weighted mean pooling over the last-layer VLM hidden states," assigning higher weights to later tokens. The formula weights each token position i proportionally to its sequence position, enabling the model to emphasize information appearing toward the end of the sequence.

**Similarity and Loss:**
Retrieval relevance is determined by cosine similarity between query and document embeddings. The model optimizes using InfoNCE loss, contrasting positive documents against negative examples within training batches.

## Generation Strategies

VisRAG-Gen proposes three mechanisms for handling multiple retrieved pages:

**Page Concatenation:** Horizontally combines multiple document images into a single image, accommodating VLMs designed for single-image input.

**Weighted Selection:** Generates answers for each retrieved page independently, selecting the final response using a weighted confidence metric combining generation probability and normalized retrieval scores.

**Multi-Image VLMs:** Leverages models like MiniCPM-V 2.6 and GPT-4o that natively support multiple image inputs for cross-page reasoning.

## Training Data and Objectives

The training dataset combines visual question-answering benchmarks (MP-DocVQA, ArXivQA, ChartQA, InfographicsVQA, PlotQA, SlideVQA) with synthetically generated query-document pairs. Authors "collect openly available PDFs from online sources and generate queries using GPT-4o," sourcing approximately 40,000 pages from textbooks, research papers, and product manuals.

VisRAG-Ret trains for a single epoch with batch size 128 on eight A100 GPUs, using temperature 0.02 for the contrastive loss. Importantly, generation components use off-the-shelf VLMs without fine-tuning.

## Key Technical Advantage

By preserving document images throughout the pipeline, "VisRAG maximizes the retention and utilization of the data information in the original documents, eliminating the information loss introduced during the parsing process."

# RegionRAG: Technical Architecture and Methods

## Overview
RegionRAG is a document understanding system that operates at the region level rather than processing entire pages holistically. The approach combines retrieval-augmented generation with region-based processing to improve visual document comprehension.

## Core Architecture

### Region Definition and Extraction
The system segments documents into meaningful regions using layout analysis. Regions represent coherent content blocks (text, tables, figures) rather than uniform patches. This granular approach allows the model to reason about document structure more effectively than page-level methods.

### Hybrid Supervision Strategy
RegionRAG employs a dual-supervision approach during training:

1. **Region-level supervision**: Direct training signals guide the model to identify and process relevant regions correctly
2. **Document-level supervision**: End-to-end objectives ensure the final outputs answer queries accurately

This hybrid approach balances learning fine-grained region understanding with maintaining overall document comprehension goals.

## Dynamic Patch Grouping at Inference

Rather than fixed spatial divisions, the system dynamically groups image patches into coherent regions during inference. This adaptive approach:

- Respects document layout structure
- Groups patches belonging to the same content block
- Enables efficient processing of variable-length regions
- Improves computational efficiency compared to processing all patches uniformly

## Retriever Component

The retriever component identifies relevant regions from documents. It operates as follows:

- Encodes document regions into dense representations
- Compares encoded regions against query embeddings
- Ranks and retrieves top-K most relevant regions
- Provides context for the generator

## Generator Component

The generator produces answers based on retrieved regions:

- Accepts concatenated region features as input
- Generates textual responses answering document queries
- Trained with standard language modeling objectives
- Benefits from focused context via regional retrieval

## Training Objectives

The system combines multiple loss functions:

1. **Retrieval loss**: Guides region ranking to match ground-truth relevant regions
2. **Generation loss**: Standard cross-entropy loss for answer prediction
3. **Joint optimization**: Alternates or jointly optimizes both components

The multi-objective training ensures regions are correctly identified while maintaining generation quality.

## Key Innovation

The region-level approach contrasts with token-level or page-level alternatives by operating at semantically meaningful content boundaries, improving both efficiency and accuracy for document question-answering tasks.

# Nemotron ColEmbed V2: Method and Training Details

## Architecture Overview

Nemotron ColEmbed V2 implements a **late interaction embedding model** for visual document retrieval. The system uses "bidirectional attention" mechanisms to process document images and query text, enabling token-level matching rather than dense vector comparison alone.

## Key Technical Components

**Late Interaction Mechanism:**
The model employs a pooling strategy that defers similarity computation until the final matching stage. Rather than collapsing embeddings immediately, token-level representations are preserved, allowing fine-grained query-document alignment during retrieval.

**Cluster-Based Sampling:**
Training utilizes cluster-based negative sampling strategies to construct challenging training batches. This technique groups similar documents together, enabling the model to distinguish between semantically related yet distinct documents—a critical capability for document retrieval tasks.

**Hard-Negative Mining:**
The training pipeline incorporates hard-negative mining, specifically selecting difficult negative examples that are nearly relevant but ultimately irrelevant. This targets the model's weakest areas during training.

## Model Variants and Training

The architecture is implemented across three model sizes:
- 3B parameter variant (LLaMA-based NeMoRetriever)
- 4B parameter variant (vision-language focused)
- 8B parameter variant (larger capacity)

## Training Data and Approach

Models are trained on diverse document retrieval datasets, including "MIRACL-Vision" benchmarks for multilingual visual document understanding. Training emphasizes both English and cross-lingual capabilities.

**Data integration** combines text-based retrieval datasets with visual document collections, enabling the model to handle both modalities effectively during inference.

# Nemotron ColEmbed V2: Complete Methods Overview

## Bidirectional Attention Implementation

The authors modified decoder LLMs to function as encoders by converting causal attention to bidirectional attention. Specifically, they note: "When adapting decoder LLMs as embedding models (encoders), a common practice involves transitioning the uni-directional attention to bi-directional attention." This enables tokens to integrate information from both preceding and succeeding positions, enhancing retrieval accuracy.

## Hard-Negative Mining Strategy

The approach uses an internal Eagle 3B VLM model to extract similar negatives from the corpus. They employ "the top-k with percentage to positive threshold method" with a 0.95 threshold, selecting the k most relevant negative samples whose similarity scores remain below 95% of the positive sample similarity. This filtering prevents false negatives (actually positive examples) from being incorrectly treated as negatives.

## Cluster-Based Data Sampling Process

The sampling workflow involves several stages:
1. Generate embeddings from document pages using an internal Eagle VLM (3072-dim vectors)
2. Apply PCA reduction to 50 dimensions
3. Apply K-Means with gap statistics to identify optimal cluster count
4. Perform uniform sampling across discovered clusters (14 identified clusters)
5. Collect queries and associated negatives from sampled positives

## Late Interaction Mechanism

The MaxSim scoring operates by having "each token embedding interact with all document token embeddings using a MaxSim operator, which selects the maximum similarity per query token and sums these scores to produce the final relevance score." This enables fine-grained matching while allowing pre-computed document embeddings.

## Model Merging Approach

The technique combines weights from multiple models trained with different data blends and hyperparameters. The 3B variant merges 8 models; the 4B and 8B variants each merge 4 models. Improvements observed: 0.8% (3B), 1.0% (4B), and 1.5% (8B).

## Training Pipeline Components

**Cross-lingual Translation**: Queries are translated using Qwen3-235B across six languages to expand training diversity.

**Two-stage Training** (3B model only):
- Stage 1: Text-only corpus training
- Stage 2: Image corpus fine-tuning

**Single-stage Training** (4B, 8B): Direct image corpus contrastive learning leveraging stronger pre-training.

**Loss Function**: The InfoNCE contrastive loss maximizes similarity between query-positive pairs while minimizing query-negative similarity, scaled by temperature parameter τ.

# RegionRAG Method Section: Technical Overview

## Architecture and Components

RegionRAG consists of two main components: a **RegionRetriever** (ℛ) that identifies relevant patches from documents using a shared vision-language model, and a **Generator** (𝒢) that synthesizes answers conditioned on retrieved regions and queries.

## Training Strategy: Dual-Level Alignment

The framework employs two complementary supervision objectives:

### 1. Global Document-Query Alignment

This stage enables document-level retrieval. The method segments documents into N non-overlapping patches, extracting embeddings E_D = {e₁, e₂, ..., e_N}. A global representation v_D is created via "element-wise max-pooling operation across the N patch embeddings."

The global contrastive loss uses InfoNCE:

**ℒ_global = -1/b ∑ᵢ₌₁ᵇ log(exp(s(e_qᵢ, v_Dᵢ)/τ) / ∑ⱼ₌₁ᵇ exp(s(e_qᵢ, v_Dⱼ)/τ))**

Where s denotes cosine similarity and τ is a temperature parameter (0.02 for global loss).

### 2. Fine-Grained Region-Query Alignment

This stage pinpoints query-relevant patches within documents through hybrid supervision.

#### Labeled Data Supervision

For documents with ground-truth bounding boxes, the method constructs:
- **Positive set P⁺ᵢ**: patches whose centers fall within any ground-truth box
- **Negative set P⁻ᵢ**: patches entirely outside ground-truth boxes

#### Unlabeled Data Supervision

For unannotated data, the approach generates pseudo-labels by computing a saliency map capturing query-patch similarity. A threshold θ (set to 0) binarizes this map: patches with similarity above θ become positive examples; below become negative.

#### Unified Local Loss

Both supervision types share a single contrastive formulation:

**ℒ_local = -log(∑_p∈P⁺ᵢ exp(s(e_qᵢ, p)/τ) / ∑_p∈{P⁺ᵢ,P⁻ᵢ} exp(s(e_qᵢ, p)/τ))**

Temperature τ = 0.25 for local loss.

### Combined Objective

**ℒ_RegionRAG = α·ℒ_global + β·ℒ_local**

Where α = 1 and β = 0.01 (weighting coefficients).

## Inference: Region Proposal and Grouping

### Saliency Mapping

The retriever computes similarity scores between query embedding e_q and all patch embeddings, generating a 2D saliency map S. This map is binarized using threshold η:

**M_k = {1 if S_k ≥ η; 0 if S_k < η}**

### Neighbor-Based Patch Grouping

The algorithm groups salient patches into connected components using "Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm for efficient traversal." Connectivity is determined by Chebyshev distance:

**D((x₁,y₁), (x₂,y₂)) = max(|x₁−x₂|, |y₁−y₂|)**

Two patches connect if their distance ≤ neighborhood radius r (optimal r=1). The algorithm maintains a queue for BFS traversal, marking visited patches to avoid redundancy.

### Bounding Box Generation

For each identified connected component, the method computes the minimum bounding rectangle by finding extremal grid coordinates, then converts these to pixel coordinates on the original image.

## Key Architectural Details

- **Base Model**: Qwen2.5-VL-3B initialized for RegionRetriever; Generator is off-the-shelf (unfine-tuned)
- **Training**: 220k combined samples (98k labeled, 122k unlabeled); 5 epochs; batch size 64
- **Parameter Efficiency**: LoRA fine-tuning with rank r=32, α_l=32, dropout 0.1
- **Optimizer**: AdamW with learning rate 2e-4

The hybrid supervision strategy proves critical: ablations show removing labeled data causes "dramatic drop in R@1...far greater than removing unlabeled data," while the reverse holds for other datasets, indicating complementary signal types.

# HybriDLA: Technical Method Overview

## Architecture Framework

HybriDLA comprises two main components: a multi-scale feature fusion encoder and a hybrid generative decoder operating within a coarse-to-fine pipeline.

## Multi-Scale Feature-Fusion Encoder

The encoder transforms multi-scale feature maps into a unified spatial-aware representation through two stages:

**Local Feature Encoding**: Each feature map F_l undergoes local enrichment via combined self-attention and convolutional operations, producing H_l. This captures both long-range dependencies and local patterns while preserving fine-grained details.

**Cross-Scale Fusion**: An attention-based fusion function Ψ merges information across scales adaptively. Features at different scales exchange information bidirectionally—fine details incorporate global context from coarse maps and vice versa. Lateral convolutions align features into a common space, generating final representation G.

## Hybrid Generative Decoder

The decoder unifies two complementary mechanisms operating simultaneously:

### Autoregressive Query Expansion (AQE)

This component generates variable-length region query sequences autoregressively:

P(Q|X) = ∏P(q_t|X, q_<t) · P(EOS|X, q_1:N)

Each decoder layer D_θ,t conditions on image features X and previously generated queries. At each step, the model proposes the next query q_t contextually, eventually emitting an end-of-sequence (EOS) token to adaptively halt expansion. The data-dependent cardinality N flexibly accommodates documents with varying element counts—more queries for complex layouts, fewer for simple documents.

### Diffusion-Based Refinement (DR)

Rather than injecting noise like standard diffusion models, this mechanism treats predictions as noisy estimates and applies iterative residual corrections:

ŷ^(t+1) = ŷ^(t) + Δ^(t)

Each decoder layer predicts residuals Δ^(t) focusing on error correction. Self-attention shares contextual information among queries while cross-attention integrates visual features, enabling precise localized updates. Feed-forward networks apply learned residuals yielding refined predictions ŷ^(t+1).

**Training Strategy**: Denoising queries are initialized with perturbed ground-truth layouts. Auxiliary losses at each decoder layer supervise intermediate predictions y^(t), forcing convergence while maintaining theoretical accuracy.

## Handling Variable Element Counts

The autoregressive expansion dynamically adjusts query counts hierarchically. Initial coarse queries capture major regions; subsequent layers spawn new queries targeting sub-elements within coarse regions. The learned stopping criterion P(EOS|X, q_1:N) assesses whether current queries sufficiently explain the document layout, continuing expansion if unexplained regions remain.

## Key Architectural Details

- **Feature Representation**: G provides both initial coarse proposals and multi-scale guidance for decoder-generated queries
- **Decoder Depth**: Typically 6 layers; deeper decoders extract more value from iterative refinement
- **Query Budget**: Approximately 300 initial queries and 300 autoregressively expanded queries yield optimal stability
- **Intermediate Supervision**: Auxiliary heads at each layer enable fast convergence
- **Attention Mechanisms**: Self-attention enables query communication; cross-attention integrates visual features

The architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance (83.5% mAP on DocLayNet with InternImage backbone) by combining coarse structure identification with progressive detail refinement, mirroring human document reading strategies.

## Model Architecture

**Three model variants:**
- **8B model**: Built on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (8.8B parameters, 4096 embedding dim)
- **4B model**: Built on Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (4.8B parameters, 2560 embedding dim)
- **3B model**: Built on Llama-3.2-3B + SigLIP2-giant (4.4B parameters, 3072 embedding dim)

### Architecture Modifications

1. **Bidirectional Self-Attention**: Replaced the original uni-directional causal self-attention from LLM decoders with bi-directional attention, enabling rich representations from whole input sequences

2. **ColBERT-Style Late Interaction**: Each input token outputs an n-dimensional embedding vector (where n = model's hidden size), enabling fine-grained multi-vector interactions via the **MaxSim operator**:
   - Each query token embedding interacts with all document token embeddings
   - MaxSim selects maximum similarity for each query token
   - Final score = sum of these maxima

## Training Methodology

### Training Architecture
- **Bi-encoder**: Query and document encoded independently
- **Contrastive Learning**: Maximizes similarity between query and relevant documents while minimizing similarity to negative documents

### Training Pipeline

**3B model (two-stage):**
1. Fine-tuned with 12.5M text-QA pairs
2. Fine-tuned with text-image pairs

**4B & 8B models:**
- Fine-tuned using text-image pairs only

- Training datasets contain both text-only and text-image pairs
